name: Outbound LinkedIn DM Rubric for xAI Roles (Hard)
description: Score an outbound LinkedIn DM. Designed to reward genuine personalization and penalize templated or copy-paste outreach. Max score ~37 before penalties.

sections.title: Relevance & Fit
criteria: +3 references SPECIFIC role requirements from JD (not just 'AI' or 'engineering')
+3 connects candidate's background to role in a non-obvious way (not just keyword matching)
penalties: -3 seniority mismatch (e.g., pitching IC role to director-level candidate)
-3 role requirements don't match candidate's actual background

sections.title: Genuine Personalization
criteria: +4 references a SPECIFIC project/achievement with detail (company name, metric, technology)
+3 draws a non-obvious connection between candidate's work and role needs
+3 shows evidence of actually reading the profile (not just keyword extraction)
penalties: -5 generic phrases that could apply to anyone ('your impressive background', 'your experience')
-4 copy-pastes or closely paraphrases text from the candidate profile
-3 mentions skills/projects without connecting them to why they matter for THIS role
-2 uses candidate's name but nothing else specific

sections.title: Compelling Value Proposition
criteria: +3 explains what makes THIS role uniquely interesting (not generic 'great company')
+3 addresses likely candidate objections or concerns proactively
penalties: -2 value prop could apply to any company/role

sections.title: Call to Action
criteria: +2 clear, specific CTA (not just 'let me know')
+2 low-friction ask (quick call, not 'send your resume')
penalties: -2 no clear CTA or multiple conflicting asks

sections.title: Tone & Authenticity
criteria: +2 sounds like a human, not a template
+2 confident but not pushy or desperate
+1 appropriate level of formality for LinkedIn

global_penalties: -6 hallucinated facts about candidate (wrong company, fake project, wrong name)
-5 hallucinated facts about role (wrong title, made-up requirements)
-4 message is clearly a template with blanks filled in
-3 over 150 words (LinkedIn DMs should be scannable)
-2 under 50 words (too brief to be compelling)
scoring_notes: Be a harsh grader. Real recruiters send templated spam constantly — the bar for 'good' is much higher than 'has the right keywords'. A score of 25+ should be rare and indicate genuinely thoughtful outreach. Most mediocre messages should score 12-18. Templated messages should score <10.
